library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Stemkens_2024_clofazimine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Stemkens_2024_clofazimine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkae309> (open access, PMC11638672)
* Supplement: Supplementary data at JAC Online (Text S3 holds the final NONMEM
  control stream)

Clofazimine has a very large volume of distribution and a terminal half-life
of months, so plasma concentrations take most of a year to approach steady
state at the standard 100 mg once-daily dose. Stemkens et al. studied a
4-week 300 mg once-daily loading phase (the C-LOAD study), pooled the data
with the PERC trial (100 mg once daily without loading), and used the
resulting population PK model to simulate alternative loading regimens.

# Population

C-LOAD enrolled 12 adults with pulmonary (9) or extrapulmonary (3)
nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) disease at Radboud University Medical
Center, Nijmegen, the Netherlands: median age 69 years (range 39-82), median
body weight 62 kg (51-105), median fat-free mass 50 kg (38-70), 50% male, 10
Caucasian and 2 Middle Eastern participants (Table 1). Most had *M. avium*
complex disease and all received other antimycobacterial drugs (azithromycin
in 11, ethambutol in 9, intravenous amikacin in 8, rifampicin in 7). The 19
PERC participants had *M. avium* complex pulmonary disease and received 100
mg once daily; their demographics are not tabulated in this paper. The model
was fitted to 112 C-LOAD and 67 PERC concentrations.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Stemkens_2024_clofazimine")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. Table
4 of the paper and the Text S3 control stream agree on all fixed effects; the
table below collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL/F, 70 kg) | log(4.17 L/h) | Table 4; Text S3 THETA(1) |
| `lvc` (V/F, 70 kg) | log(460 L) | Table 4; Text S3 THETA(2) |
| `lka` (absorption and transit rate) | log(0.683 1/h) | Table 4; Text S3 THETA(3), used for K12 and K23 |
| `lq` (Q/F, 70 kg) | log(24.6 L/h) | Table 4; Text S3 THETA(4) |
| `lvp` (Vp/F, 70 kg) | log(10100 L) | Table 4; Text S3 THETA(5) |
| `lfdepot` | log(1), fixed | Text S3 `F1 = 1*IOVF*highdoseEFF` |
| `e_dose_high_fdepot` | 0.736 | Table 4 'Effect of high-dose on bioavailability' 73.6%; Text S3 THETA(6) |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Table 4 footnote b; Text S3 `AlloCL`, `AlloV` |
| `etalcl` | 0.55 | Text S3 $OMEGA; Table 4 IIV CL 85.6% CV |
| `etalka` | 0.501 | Text S3 $OMEGA; Table 4 IIV absorption-rate constant 80.6% CV |
| `etaiov_fdepot_1..3` | 0.488 (2 and 3 fixed equal) | Text S3 $OMEGA BLOCK(1) + 2 x SAME; Table 4 IOV F 79.3% CV |
| `propSd` | 0.08 | Table 4 'Proportional error' 8.00%; Text S3 $SIGMA 0.00639 |
| `addSd` | 0.0417 mg/L | Text S3 $SIGMA 0.00174 (variance); see Assumptions |
| Allometric scaling | `(WT/70)^0.75` on CL, Q; `(WT/70)^1` on V, Vp | Text S3 $PK |
| ODEs | depot -> transit1 -> central <-> peripheral1, both absorption steps at `ka` | Text S3 $MODEL / ADVAN5 rate constants; Figure S1 |
| `f(depot)` | `exp(lfdepot + iov) * 0.736^DOSE_HIGH` | Text S3 $PK |
| Residual error | `Cc * (1 + eps1) + eps2` | Text S3 $ERROR |

The CV% values of Table 4 are reproduced from the control-stream variances
with the paper's own formula (footnote c, CV = sqrt(exp(omega) - 1)):

```{r cv-check}
omega <- c(etalcl = 0.55, etalka = 0.501, etaiov_fdepot = 0.488)
cv_model <- round(100 * sqrt(exp(omega) - 1), 1)
cv_table4 <- c(etalcl = 85.6, etalka = 80.6, etaiov_fdepot = 79.3)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  random_effect = names(omega), variance = omega,
  cv_from_variance = cv_model, cv_table4 = cv_table4
), row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(abs(cv_model - cv_table4) < 0.15))
```

# Model structure check: terminal half-life

The paper's Discussion quotes a terminal half-life of about 80 days. The
typical-value micro-constants of the packaged model (70 kg) give:

```{r half-life}
mod <- readModelDb("Stemkens_2024_clofazimine")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- exp(ui$theta[c("lcl", "lvc", "lq", "lvp")])
k10 <- th[["lcl"]] / th[["lvc"]]
k12 <- th[["lq"]] / th[["lvc"]]
k21 <- th[["lq"]] / th[["lvp"]]
s <- k10 + k12 + k21
beta <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
thalf_days <- log(2) / beta / 24
thalf_days
stopifnot(thalf_days > 70, thalf_days < 95)
```

# Solver settings

A daily oral dose over most of a year combined with a sharp absorption peak and
an 85-day terminal phase exhausts LSODA's default step budget ("could not solve
the system"). Every long simulation below caps the step at 4 h and raises the
step limit; steady-state (`ss = 1`) solves also raise `maxSS`, because the
slow phase needs many dosing intervals to converge.

```{r solver}
solve_long <- function(model, events, ...) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    model,
    events = events,
    hmax = 4,
    maxsteps = 1e6,
    maxSS = 20000,
    returnType = "data.frame",
    ...
  )
}
```

# Replicate Figure 3: typical-patient trough profiles

Figure 3 shows simulated trough (pre-dose) concentrations for a typical 65 kg
patient on three regimens, with a dashed target line at 80% of the
"predicted steady-state trough". Inter-occasion variability is switched off
by setting `OCC = 0` on every record, and the doses are labelled with
`DOSE_HIGH` (1 for 300 mg, 0 for 100 mg).

```{r regimen-events}
horizon_days <- 336 # 48 weeks, the end of the Figure 3 time axis (about 11 months)

make_regimen <- function(id, loading_dose, loading_weeks, wt, regimen,
                         ndays = horizon_days) {
  day <- 0:ndays
  dose_day <- day[day < ndays]
  amt <- ifelse(dose_day < loading_weeks * 7, loading_dose, 100)
  doses <- tibble(
    id = id, time = dose_day * 24, evid = 1L, amt = amt, cmt = "depot",
    DOSE_HIGH = as.integer(amt == 300)
  )
  # One trough record per day, placed BEFORE that day's dose (evid 0 sorts
  # first at a shared time), so the value is the pre-dose concentration.
  troughs <- tibble(
    id = id, time = day * 24, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "central",
    DOSE_HIGH = NA_integer_
  )
  bind_rows(troughs, doses) |>
    arrange(id, time, evid) |>
    tidyr::fill(DOSE_HIGH, .direction = "up") |>
    mutate(DOSE_HIGH = tidyr::replace_na(DOSE_HIGH, 0L), WT = wt, OCC = 0L,
           regimen = regimen)
}

regimens <- tibble(
  regimen = c("100 mg once daily", "300 mg once daily 4 weeks",
              "300 mg once daily 6 weeks", "300 mg once daily 8 weeks"),
  loading_dose = c(100, 300, 300, 300),
  loading_weeks = c(0, 4, 6, 8)
)
```

```{r figure-3}
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
ev_typical <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_regimen(i, regimens$loading_dose[i], regimens$loading_weeks[i],
               wt = 65, regimen = regimens$regimen[i])
}))
sim_typical <- solve_long(mod_typical, ev_typical, keep = "regimen") |>
  mutate(months = time / 24 / 30.4375)

# True steady-state trough at 100 mg once daily (ss = 1), 65 kg.
ev_ss <- tibble(
  id = 1L, time = c(0, 24), evid = c(1L, 0L), amt = c(100, NA),
  ii = c(24, 0), ss = c(1L, 0L), cmt = c("depot", "central"),
  WT = 65, OCC = 0L, DOSE_HIGH = 0L
)
trough_ss_true <- solve_long(mod_typical, ev_ss)$Cc[1]
trough_end <- sim_typical |>
  filter(regimen == "100 mg once daily", time == horizon_days * 24) |>
  pull(Cc)
target_typical <- 0.8 * trough_end
c(true_steady_state = trough_ss_true, end_of_horizon = trough_end,
  target = target_typical)

sim_typical |>
  filter(regimen != "300 mg once daily 8 weeks") |>
  ggplot(aes(months, Cc, colour = regimen, linetype = regimen)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = target_typical, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of treatment (months)",
    y = "Simulated clofazimine trough concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = "Loading dose regimen", linetype = "Loading dose regimen",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Stemkens 2024 (typical 65 kg patient)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The 100 mg curve ends near 0.93 mg/L at 11 months and the 6-week loading
curve peaks at about 0.75 mg/L at the end of loading, as in Figure 3. The
dashed target line of Figure 3 sits at about 0.74 mg/L, which is 80% of the
trough at the **end of the 11-month simulation** (`r round(trough_end, 3)`
mg/L), not 80% of the true steady-state trough (`r round(trough_ss_true, 3)`
mg/L): with an 85-day half-life the 100 mg regimen is still about 6% short
of steady state at 11 months. The time-to-target replication below therefore
uses the end-of-horizon trough as the "steady-state" reference, which is what
reproduces the published numbers.

```{r figure-3-checks}
end_loading <- sim_typical |>
  inner_join(regimens, by = "regimen") |>
  filter(time == loading_weeks * 7 * 24, loading_weeks > 0) |>
  select(regimen, Cc)
end_loading
stopifnot(
  abs(trough_end / 0.93 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(end_loading$Cc[end_loading$regimen == "300 mg once daily 6 weeks"] / 0.75 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

```{r table-5-typical}
ttt_typical <- sim_typical |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(months_to_target = min(months[Cc >= target_typical]),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    tibble(regimen = regimens$regimen, table5_median = c(5.3, 3.8, 1.4, 1.4)),
    by = "regimen"
  )
ttt_typical |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen,
                "Typical patient, months to target" = months_to_target,
                "Table 5 median (months)" = table5_median) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(all(abs(ttt_typical$months_to_target - ttt_typical$table5_median) < 0.2))
```

The typical 65 kg patient reaches the target in 5.3, 3.8, 1.4 and 1.4 months
on the four regimens, matching the medians of Table 5 to the printed
precision. The 4-week and 6-week loading results discriminate sharply
between candidate bioavailabilities for the 300 mg dose: the 6-week regimen
reaches the target only because the trough at the end of loading just
crosses it, which requires the 0.736 relative bioavailability.

# Replicate Table 5: virtual population

The paper simulated 1000 patients per regimen with body weight log-normally
distributed "based on the combined demographics" of C-LOAD and PERC. The
parameters of that distribution are not reported; the cohort below uses a
log-normal weight with median 62 kg (the C-LOAD median) and a log-scale SD of
0.2, truncated to 45-120 kg. Each virtual patient keeps the same random
effects on every regimen (paired design), drawn in base R so the cohort is
identical on every machine, and the individual target is 80% of that
patient's own 100 mg trough at day `r horizon_days`. The cohort has 200
patients per regimen.

```{r table-5-cohort}
set.seed(20241211)
n_pat <- 200
omega_mat <- ui$omega
eta <- matrix(rnorm(n_pat * nrow(omega_mat)), n_pat) %*% chol(omega_mat)
colnames(eta) <- rownames(omega_mat)
wt_pat <- pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n_pat, log(62), 0.2)), 45), 120)

ev_pop <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_pat), function(k) {
    make_regimen((i - 1) * n_pat + k, regimens$loading_dose[i],
                 regimens$loading_weeks[i], wt = wt_pat[k],
                 regimen = regimens$regimen[i]) |>
      mutate(patient = k)
  }))
}))
params_pop <- data.frame(
  id = (rep(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), each = n_pat) - 1) * n_pat +
    rep(seq_len(n_pat), nrow(regimens)),
  eta[rep(seq_len(n_pat), nrow(regimens)), , drop = FALSE]
)
sim_pop <- solve_long(mod_typical, ev_pop, params = params_pop,
                      keep = c("regimen", "patient")) |>
  mutate(months = time / 24 / 30.4375)

targets <- sim_pop |>
  filter(regimen == "100 mg once daily", time == horizon_days * 24) |>
  transmute(patient, target = 0.8 * Cc)

ttt_pop <- sim_pop |>
  inner_join(targets, by = "patient") |>
  group_by(regimen, patient) |>
  summarise(months_to_target = min(months[Cc >= target]), .groups = "drop")

table5 <- tibble(
  regimen = regimens$regimen,
  paper = c("5.3 (0.93-8.1)", "3.8 (0.33-7.6)", "1.4 (0.30-7.3)",
            "1.4 (0.30-7.0)"),
  paper_median = c(5.3, 3.8, 1.4, 1.4)
)
ttt_summary <- ttt_pop |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(months_to_target),
    p025 = quantile(months_to_target, 0.025),
    p975 = quantile(months_to_target, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(table5, by = "regimen")
ttt_summary |>
  mutate(simulated = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f-%.1f)", median, p025, p975)) |>
  select(regimen, simulated, paper) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen,
                "Simulated, months to target, median (2.5th-97.5th)" = simulated,
                "Table 5, median (2.5th-97.5th)" = paper) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r table-5-checks}
# Typical-value medians match Table 5 exactly (above). Across a cohort the
# median moves with which patients land near the threshold, and the 4-week
# regimen sits on a shallow approach to the target, so the band is wider
# there. A wrong clearance, volume or 300 mg bioavailability shifts these
# medians by months, not tenths.
stopifnot(all(abs(ttt_summary$median - ttt_summary$paper_median) < 0.8))
```

```{r table-5-plot}
ttt_pop |>
  ggplot(aes(months_to_target, colour = regimen)) +
  stat_ecdf(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Months to 80% of individual reference trough",
       y = "Cumulative fraction of virtual patients", colour = "Regimen") +
  theme_bw()
```

The 200 mg and 400 mg loading regimens of Table 5 are not simulated: the
model's high-dose bioavailability term is defined only for the 300 mg dose
the study used (`DOSE_HIGH` contrasts 300 mg with 100 mg), and the paper does
not report how bioavailability was extrapolated to 200 mg and 400 mg.

# PKNCA validation: model-derived exposure (Table S5)

Table S5 reports geometric means of model-derived AUC0-24h, Cmax, Tmax and
Ctrough at the sampling visits of both studies. The virtual cohorts below
follow the two designs: C-LOAD takes 300 mg once daily for 28 days and then
100 mg once daily; PERC takes 100 mg once daily from day 0. Each sampled
dosing interval is simulated densely, with that day's dose carrying its own
inter-occasion bioavailability eta, as in the source data set (`OCC` 1-3 in
C-LOAD, 1-2 in PERC; 0 on every other dose). Body weight follows the same
distribution as above for both studies.

```{r nca-cohort}
nca_grid <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24)

make_study <- function(id, study, wt, ndays = 125) {
  dose_day <- 0:(ndays - 1)
  if (study == "C-LOAD") {
    amt <- ifelse(dose_day < 28, 300, 100)
    occ_days <- c(27, 28, 121) # last 300 mg dose, first 100 mg dose, month 4
  } else {
    amt <- rep(100, length(dose_day))
    occ_days <- c(30, 121) # month 1, month 4
  }
  occ <- match(dose_day, occ_days, nomatch = 0L)
  doses <- tibble(
    id = id, time = dose_day * 24, evid = 1L, amt = amt, cmt = "depot",
    DOSE_HIGH = as.integer(amt == 300), OCC = occ
  )
  obs <- tibble(day = rep(occ_days, each = length(nca_grid)),
                tad = rep(nca_grid, length(occ_days))) |>
    mutate(id = id, time = day * 24 + tad, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_,
           cmt = "central", DOSE_HIGH = NA_integer_, OCC = NA_integer_)
  bind_rows(obs, doses) |>
    arrange(id, time, evid) |>
    tidyr::fill(DOSE_HIGH, OCC, .direction = "up") |>
    tidyr::fill(DOSE_HIGH, OCC, .direction = "down") |>
    mutate(WT = wt, study = study)
}

n_study <- 200
ev_nca <- bind_rows(
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_study), function(k) make_study(k, "C-LOAD", wt_pat[k]))),
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_study), function(k) {
    make_study(n_study + k, "PERC", wt_pat[k])
  }))
)
# OCC on an observation row does not enter the model (bioavailability is
# evaluated at the dose); the fill above only keeps the column complete.
params_nca <- data.frame(id = seq_len(2 * n_study),
                         eta[rep(seq_len(n_study), 2), , drop = FALSE])
sim_nca_raw <- solve_long(mod_typical, ev_nca, params = params_nca,
                          keep = "study")
```

```{r nca}
visit_map <- tibble(
  study = c("C-LOAD", "C-LOAD", "C-LOAD", "PERC", "PERC"),
  day = c(27, 28, 121, 30, 121),
  treatment = c("C-LOAD day 28 (300 mg)", "C-LOAD 1 month (100 mg)",
                "C-LOAD 4 months (100 mg)", "PERC 1 month (100 mg)",
                "PERC 4 months (100 mg)")
)
# Each visit is the 24 h interval starting at that day's dose; the C-LOAD
# day-27 and day-28 intervals share the record at 28 days, hence distinct().
conc_nca <- sim_nca_raw |>
  inner_join(visit_map, by = "study", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(tad = time - day * 24) |>
  filter(tad >= 0, tad <= 24, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, tad, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(id, treatment, time = tad, Cc)
dose_nca <- conc_nca |>
  distinct(id, treatment) |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = ifelse(grepl("300 mg", treatment), 300, 100))

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE,
                        tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))

gm <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x)))
# Tmax is summarised by its median: near steady state some virtual patients
# have a nearly flat profile whose maximum is the pre-dose sample (Tmax = 0),
# and a single zero sends a geometric mean to 0.
sim_gm <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "tmax", "cmin")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(
    PPORRES = if (PPTESTCD[1] == "tmax") median(PPORRES) else gm(PPORRES),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

table_s5 <- tibble(
  treatment = visit_map$treatment,
  auclast = c(16.0, 14.6, 19.8, 7.75, 15.8),
  cmax = c(0.832, 0.734, 0.930, 0.399, 0.767),
  tmax = c(4.28, 3.93, 3.76, 4.99, 5.26),
  cmin = c(0.507, 0.517, 0.716, 0.233, 0.499)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_gm, table_s5, by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", cmax = "mg/L", tmax = "h", cmin = "mg/L")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Simulated geometric means (200 virtual patients per study) against the",
  "Table S5 model-derived geometric means (simulated Tmax is the median).",
  "Ctrough of Table S5 is compared with the minimum concentration over the",
  "dosing interval."
))
attr(cmp, "footnote")
```

```{r nca-checks}
ratio <- sim_gm |>
  inner_join(tidyr::pivot_longer(table_s5, -treatment, names_to = "PPTESTCD",
                                 values_to = "ref"),
             by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "cmin")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / ref - 1))
stopifnot(
  # Centre: a mis-transcribed clearance, dose or bioavailability moves every
  # exposure metric by tens of percent.
  abs(median(ratio$pct_diff)) < 15,
  # Envelope: the Table S5 means come from 8-19 patients per visit with an
  # 85% CV on clearance, so single cells carry wide sampling error.
  quantile(abs(ratio$pct_diff), 0.9) < 35
)
```

The geometric means of Table S5 come from the empirical Bayes estimates of
8 to 19 patients per visit, with 95% confidence intervals spanning roughly
+/-25%; a virtual cohort of 200 with assumed weights is compared against them
on the centre of the distribution. The observed geometric means of Table 2
(C-LOAD day 28: Cmax 0.87 mg/L, Ctrough 0.50 mg/L, AUC0-24h 16.1 mg*h/L;
highest measured concentration 0.75 and 0.93 mg/L at 1 and 4 months in
C-LOAD and 0.39 and 0.78 mg/L in PERC) are close to the Table S5 values and
lead to the same conclusion.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Additive residual error.** Table 4 prints the additive error as 0.00174
  mg/L, but the same number appears in the Text S3 `$SIGMA` block, where
  NONMEM reads it as a variance. The proportional term confirms that Table 4
  reports `$SIGMA` on the SD scale (sqrt(0.00639) = 0.080 = the printed
  8.00%), so the additive SD is taken from the control stream as
  sqrt(0.00174) = 0.0417 mg/L. The printed 0.00174 mg/L as an SD would be
  under 4% of the assay's 0.05 mg/L lower calibration limit.
* **High-dose bioavailability covariate.** The control stream uses a
  `highdose` flag that is not in its `$INPUT` list; the Results describe the
  contrast as 300 mg versus 100 mg doses. It is encoded per dose record as
  `DOSE_HIGH` (1 for a 300 mg dose). The packaged model does not extrapolate
  to other dose levels, so the 200 mg and 400 mg rows of Table 5 are not
  replicated.
* **Inter-occasion variability on bioavailability** applies only to doses
  given on PK sampling days (`OCC` 1-3), as in the source data set; `OCC =
  0` doses have none. Simulations of new regimens set `OCC = 0` throughout.
  Whether the paper's regimen simulations included this term is not stated;
  it has no effect on the typical-value results above.
* **"Steady-state" reference for time to target.** The target is computed
  from the 100 mg trough at day 336 (48 weeks, the end of the Figure 3
  axis) rather than the true steady state, because that is what reproduces
  both the Figure 3 target line and the Table 5 medians. The exact
  simulation horizon is not reported; a month is taken as 30.4375 days.
* **Virtual-population body weight.** Log-normal with median 62 kg and
  log-scale SD 0.2, truncated to 45-120 kg; the paper's distribution
  parameters are not reported, and PERC demographics are not tabulated.
* **Ctrough in the NCA table** is compared with the PKNCA minimum
  concentration over the 24 h interval; Table S5 does not state whether its
  Ctrough is the pre-dose or end-of-interval value, which differ little near
  steady state.
* **Tmax summary.** Table S5 labels its Tmax as a geometric mean; the
  simulated Tmax is summarised by the median, because virtual patients with a
  flat steady-state profile have Tmax = 0 and a geometric mean of 0.
* **Covariates screened and not retained** (rifampicin co-administration,
  age, sex, pulmonary versus extrapulmonary disease, study) are recorded in
  the model's `covariatesDataExcluded` metadata.
